jp: 今年[ことし]{は|wa-topic}桜[さくら]{が|ga-subject}早[はや]く咲[さ]く{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard the cherry blossoms will bloom early this year.
why: Sentence-final って after a plain verb marks the sentence as something heard from someone else.

jp: 山田[やまだ]さん{は|wa-topic}毎週[まいしゅう]プール{で|de-place}泳[およ]いでいる{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard Mr. Yamada swims at the pool every week.
why: Plain-form verb plus って passes on information that someone else told you.

jp: 来週[らいしゅう]{の|no-possessive}マラソン大会[たいかい]{は|wa-topic}中止[ちゅうし]{だって|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard next week's marathon has been cancelled.
why: After a noun, the hearsay marker is だって: it reports what you were told.

jp: あの選手[せんしゅ]{は|wa-topic}足[あし]{を|o-object}けがした{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard that player got a leg injury.
why: って after a plain past verb reports a secondhand fact, not the speaker's own observation.

jp: 森[もり]{の|no-possessive}中[なか]{で|de-place}珍[めずら]しい鳥[とり]{が|ga-subject}見[み]つかった{って|tte-hearsay}。

why: Plain past form plus って marks the news as heard from someone else.

jp: 山[やま]{の|no-possessive}上[うえ]{は|wa-topic}もう寒[さむ]い{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard it's already cold at the top of the mountain.
why: Attached directly to an い-adjective, sentence-final って reports what you were told.

jp: 佐藤[さとう]さん{は|wa-topic}最近[さいきん]ヨガ{に|ni-destination}通[かよ]っている{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard Mr. Sato has been going to yoga classes lately.

jp: 隣[となり]{の|no-possessive}おじさん{は|wa-topic}来月[らいげつ]ゴルフ{を|o-object}始[はじ]める{って|tte-hearsay}。

jp: 犬[いぬ]{の|no-possessive}散歩[さんぽ]{は|wa-topic}朝[あさ]{より|yori-comparison}夕方[ゆうがた]{が|ga-subject}いい{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard that evening is better than morning for walking a dog.

jp: 木村[きむら]さん{は|wa-topic}風邪[かぜ]{を|o-object}引[ひ]いた{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard Mr. Kimura caught a cold.
why: A plain past verb plus って reports news you heard from another person.

jp: あの山[やま]{は|wa-topic}冬[ふゆ]{でも|demo-even}登[のぼ]れる{って|tte-hearsay}。

jp: この川[かわ]{で|de-place}六月[ろくがつ]{に|ni-time}ホタル{が|ga-subject}見[み]られる{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard fireflies can be seen at this river in June.
why: って after a plain verb tells the listener the information is secondhand.

jp: 今年[ことし]{の|no-possessive}冬[ふゆ]{は|wa-topic}雪[ゆき]{が|ga-subject}少[すく]ない{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard there will be little snow this winter.
why: Sentence-final って after a plain い-adjective (少ない) reports what someone else said.

jp: 鈴木[すずき]さん{の|no-possessive}妹[いもうと]さん{は|wa-topic}水泳[すいえい]{が|ga-stative}得意[とくい]{だって|tte-hearsay}。

jp: 山[やま]{の|no-possessive}天気[てんき]{は|wa-topic}変[か]わりやすい{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I've heard that the weather in the mountains changes easily.

jp: 今年[ことし]{も|mo-also}花粉[かふん]{が/は|ga-subject}ひどい{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard the pollen is bad again this year.
why: って after an い-adjective marks the statement as heard from someone else.

jp: 小林[こばやし]さん{は|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]十[じゅっ]キロ走[はし]る{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard Mr. Kobayashi runs ten kilometers every morning.

jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]{は|wa-topic}天気[てんき]{が|ga-subject}よくなる{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard the weather will get better over the weekend.

jp: この湖[みずうみ]{で|de-place}釣[つ]り{が|ga-subject}できる{って|tte-hearsay}。

jp: 明日[あした]{の|no-possessive}サッカー{の|no-possessive}試合[しあい]{は|wa-topic}三時[さんじ]{から|kara-from}{だって|tte-hearsay}。

jp: ジム{は|wa-topic}夜[よる]十一時[じゅういちじ]{まで|made-until}開[あ]いている{って|tte-hearsay}。

jp: 昔[むかし]、あの人[ひと]{は|wa-topic}プロ{の|no-possessive}サッカー選手[せんしゅ]だった{って|tte-hearsay}。

jp: 近所[きんじょ]{の|no-possessive}公園[こうえん]{で|de-place}大[おお]きな木[き]{が|ga-subject}倒[たお]れた{って|tte-hearsay}。

jp: 今夜[こんや]{は|wa-topic}星[ほし]{が|ga-subject}よく見[み]える{って|tte-hearsay}。

jp: 病院[びょういん]{の|no-possessive}先生[せんせい]{は|wa-topic}とても親切[しんせつ]{だって|tte-hearsay}。
